item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The graph represents the distance and time of a hike taken by Joshua and Liam.

[Image: Line graph of distance versus time]

If they both started from the same place and walked in the same direction, at what time did they meet?
item.figure_description:
A line graph with a vertical axis labeled "Distance (kilometers)" marked from 0 to 5.5 in increments of 0.5 (labeled 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5). The horizontal axis is labeled "Time" with tick marks every 30 minutes from 8:00 to 12:30 (labeled 8:00, 8:30, 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30). Two line segments are shown:
- One labeled "Joshua" begins at (8:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (12:00, 4.5).
- One labeled "Liam" begins at (9:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (11:00, 4.5).
The two lines intersect at time 10:00 and distance approximately 2.25 kilometers.

- 1999: Cherry Cola bar reaches 20; Lemon Cola bar reaches 45.

The table shows the temperatures at various times on a certain day.

| Time | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 6 p.m. |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Temperature °C | 12 | 17 | 14 | 18 | 15 |

A graph, without a temperature scale, is drawn. Of the following, which could be the graph that shows the information given in the table?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four line graphs, labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a vertical axis labeled "Temperature (°C)" without numbers or tick marks, and a horizontal axis labeled "Time" with five evenly spaced tick marks labeled "6 a.m.", "9 a.m.", "Noon", "3 p.m.", and "6 p.m.".
- Graph A: The line begins at a low point at 6 a.m., rises to 9 a.m., rises further to a peak at Noon, drops sharply to a low point at 3 p.m., and rises slightly at 6 p.m.
- Graph B: The line begins at a moderate height at 6 a.m., rises to a peak at 9 a.m., drops at Noon, rises to an even higher peak at 3 p.m., and drops at 6 p.m. to a level higher than the value at Noon.
- Graph C: The line starts at a relatively high point at 6 a.m., drops to 9 a.m., rises to a peak at Noon, drops to 3 p.m., and continues downward at 6 p.m.
- Graph D: The line starts at a low point at 6 a.m., rises to 9 a.m., reaches a maximum at Noon, drops at 3 p.m., and drops further at 6 p.m.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
